headings.text: What actually matters in a mixer grinder under ₹7,000

cta.headline: Need a 900W-1000W heavy-use mixer for daily idli batter?
cta.sub: Our mixer grinder guide for heavy use covers 900W-1000W commercial-grade units and tilting wet grinders for South Indian kitchens.

tldr_pick: The Preethi Zodiac MG-218 (750W) is the best mixer grinder under ₹7,000 in India for most homes in 2026: a 750W motor with 110-minute rating, three jars (1.5 L, 1.0 L, 0.5 L), and a 5-year motor warranty backed by Preethi's widest service network in South India.
key_takeaways: ₹5,000–₹7,000 is the sweet spot for 750W-900W mixers — sub-₹5,000 you mostly find 500W-750W units; above ₹7,000 you pay for design flourishes rather than motor.
750W is enough for a 4-5 person household; step to 900W only if you grind idli/dosa batter twice a week or more.
The 5-year motor warranty is the real signal — Preethi publishes it; Philips and Bajaj publish 2 years. The 3-year gap matters when the motor dies.
Three jars with a 1.5 L wet-jar is the right configuration — two-jar setups force you to wash between tasks and slow down cooking.
who_for: Indian households that want a 750W-900W mixer grinder with three jars for chutneys, masalas, wet batters, and dry grinding on a budget under ₹7,000. Not aimed at commercial kitchens or commercial idli-dosa batter volumes — those need 1000W+ tilting wet grinders.
methodology: We compared 8 popular mixer grinders sold in India in 2026 in the ₹5,000–₹7,000 band against four kitchen tasks: dry-grinding masala (turmeric, coriander, chilli), wet-grinding chutney (coconut, mint, coriander), blending shakes and lassi, and making idli / dosa batter. Motor wattage, jar build quality, noise level, warranty length, and brand service network were weighted equally. Pricing is the current normal sale price on Amazon India and Flipkart; verify the exact model code on the listing before purchase.

faq.q: Is a 750W mixer enough for a family of 4-5?
faq.a: Yes for daily Indian cooking — chutneys, masalas, shakes, and small batches of idli / dosa batter. For a large family (6+) or for commercial idli-dosa batter volumes, step up to a 900W-1000W mixer or a tilting wet grinder. The 750W class is the sweet spot for Indian households in this price band.

faq.q: What's the difference between stainless steel and polycarbonate jars?
faq.a: Stainless steel jars are more durable, easier to clean, and don't absorb odours. Polycarbonate jars are lighter and cheaper, but they scratch over time and can develop a permanent residue if you grind masala in them regularly. Most 750W mixers in this price band come with a 1.5 L stainless steel wet-jar and 1.0 L / 0.5 L dry-jars.

faq.q: How long can a mixer grinder run continuously?
faq.a: Most 750W mixers in this price band have a 90-110 minute continuous run rating before they need a 15-20 minute cool-down. The Preethi Zodiac, Philips HL7701, and Sujata Powermatic all publish this number in their specs. Going past the run rating overheats the motor and shortens its life. For grinding idli batter (which takes 20-30 minutes), 750W is comfortable.

faq.q: Can I use a mixer grinder for idli and dosa batter?
faq.a: Yes, but in small batches. A 750W mixer with a 1.5 L jar can comfortably grind 500-750 g of rice + urad dal batter at a time, which is enough for 15-20 idlis. For larger batches, you need to do it in two cycles with a cool-down between. The Sujata Powermatic Plus (900W, 1.75 L jar) handles larger batches with less effort.

faq.q: How often do I need to service a mixer grinder?
faq.a: For daily Indian cooking, expect to replace the rubber gasket, the blade, and the coupler every 12-18 months. The motor itself should last 5-7 years with normal use. Most brands (Preethi, Philips, Bajaj) offer authorised service centres in tier-1 and tier-2 cities; the cost of a blade-and-gasket replacement is usually ₹300-₹500.
